spec_match.rationale: Runs the lifecycle edges the feature reshapes: close() probe/exercise, repeat startRendering, all three indefinite-length spellings, and the oncomplete/statechange log.

interactive.rationale: Four independent experiments, each one button driving real calls with tables or verdict regions.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises every experiment runs the real call and reports real results; delivered.

edge_cases.rationale: The page is the edge portfolio; it also resolves the explainer-vs-sample ambiguity (null vs Infinity vs omitted) empirically instead of guessing.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/<id> plus the exact spec anchor in see-also.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite mirrors close semantics, repeatability, and indefinite constructibility; verified executing on the live route.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Verified on headless Chromium 141 (predates Chrome 158, feature absent even behind --enable-experimental-web-platform-features) via Playwright 1.56 at desktop 1280x800 and mobile 360x740 DPR3 touch, driving every control; screenshots under /tmp/claude-0/agentB/shots/. Real outcomes on this build: close undefined; call #1 delivered all 2048 frames and call #2 rejected InvalidStateError in a stopped state; all three indefinite spellings threw (NotSupportedError, NotSupportedError, TypeError required-member); complete fired once with renderedBuffer.length 4096 and statechange traced running to closed.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry.assert covers the primary contract and the explicit fallback branch; console output is intentional and prefixed.

design_system.rationale: Only CSS variables from public/styles.css; buttons overriding background also set color; AA pairs (text-charcoal/bg-stone, bg-ivory/text-black, accent-emerald-dark on paper).

accessibility.rationale: Native controls with labels, visible focus (verified first-Tab), caption+scope tables, aria-live polite result regions.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Both viewports clean; result tables scroll in wrappers.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify the supported path on a real Chrome 158 / Canary build
openQuestions.detail: This environment's Chromium 141 lacks the surface even behind --enable-experimental-web-platform-features, so only the honest-absent branch ran. On Chrome 158 (or Canary with the feature's runtime flag) verify: close() interrupting an in-flight render, >=2 successful pulls before closure, which indefinite spelling constructs, and whether complete fires per-render-end under chunking.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Landmarks, native semantics, accessible names, visible focus, and polite live regions for asynchronous state changes.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Content sits in main/header/footer landmarks; async results land in aria-live=polite output/status elements; tables carry caption plus th scope=col; first-Tab focus visibility verified in the browser.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use intrinsically-sized grid/flex layouts (auto-fit + minmax) so panels reflow without horizontal overflow at narrow widths.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Control panels use grid-template-columns repeat(auto-fit, minmax()), tables are wrapped in overflow-x containers, and long tokens use overflow-wrap: anywhere; verified no horizontal overflow at 360px.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce error/failure outcomes programmatically, not only visually.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Real API errors (name + message) are written into aria-live output regions and colour is never the only signal (text states the outcome).

summary: Four real experiments that read differently on 141 and 158 by design - the difference is the lesson.
